name: uart-nrf52840-dk
experiment:
# Generic serial line (UART). On an nRF52840 DK the on-board J-Link exposes the
# target's UART as a virtual COM port (/dev/ttyACM0 on Linux). Received bytes
# and the step's write become timestamped "uart" packets; lines: true also
# emits one log event per received text line.
#
#   hwlab devices                      # find the port, e.g. uart/ttyACM0
#   hwlab run examples/uart-nrf52840-dk.yaml
#
# The write step is a state-changing call and needs --confirm-dangerous.
name: uart-nrf52840-dk
duration: 6s

devices:
  console:
    plugin: uart
    device: ttyACM0
    baud: 115200
    data_bits: 8
    parity: none
    stop_bits: 1
    flow_control: none
    lines: true

steps:
  - {name: say-hello, at: 2s, device: console, call: SerialTransport.write, args: {data: "hello\r\n"}}

clock.source: host clock at serial read return (rx) / before write call (tx)
clock.note: 115200 8N1 flow=none; rx 0 bytes, tx 7 bytes; the chunk stamp is the first read of the chunk, late by the unmeasured USB and driver latency
